ncei_nurdle_patrol.plastic_separable: yes by construction: every row is plastic pellets (< 5 mm) only, hand-picked
ncei_nurdle_patrol.protocol_fields: Volunteers Number (1..105, median 1), Collecting Time min (0..840; 10 min for 7,838 rows), New Tide Line yes/no (accession only)
gotchas: Standardisation is INCONSISTENT: of 10,615 rows 7,275 equal amount*10/minutes, a further 1,721 equal amount*10/(minutes*volunteers), 1,613 match neither (e.g. 47 in 5 min stored as 47) -> recompute from the raw count and effort, never store the published standardised value
6 rows with Collecting Time 0 (standardised 0 or 1) -> effort undefined, drop and count
Sample Date is local midnight written as UTC 05:00/06:00 (US Central) -> a DATE, not a time

Not only sea shores: 485 rows in inland or Great-Lakes US states (Ohio 249, Illinois 65, Pennsylvania 54, ...), 689 rows whose Location names a lake/river/creek/reservoir -> needs a freshwater qc bit from a coastline-distance test, not a state list
790 rows share date+position with another row (379 groups, 96 with identical values) - multiple patrols at one spot, not copies; keep
Lat precision varies 1-6 decimals (562 rows 3 dp, 49 rows 2 dp, 7 rows 1 dp)

emodnet_beach_litter.http: 200, 21,183,865 bytes; zip holds beach_erddap_surveys_metadata.csv (11.1 MB) and beach_erddap_surveys_litter.csv (443.7 MB). The 2026 name answers 404. licence_verbatim.erddap_global: Usage is subject to mandatory citation: "This resource was generated in the framework of EMODnet Chemistry, under the support of DG MARE Call for Tender EASME/EMFF/2020/3.1.11/European Marine Observation and Data Network (EMODnet) - Lot 5 - Chemistry"
licence_verbatim.L08_meaning: UN = 'The data are freely available to anybody and may be used for any purpose. Usage acknowledgement may be required.'; CB = 'The data are available under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International Public License'; LS = 'Access to the data and usage are as specified in the SeaDataNet data policy and licence agreement'
licence_verbatim.seadatanet_licence_clause_5: 5. Data Users should not give to third parties any SeaDataNet data or product without prior consent from the source Data Centre.
licence_verbatim.conflict: The file is named 'unrestricted' and the record says CC BY 4.0, but 8,130 of 16,861 surveys (48%) carry LS, whose licence forbids passing data to third parties without consent. mplastic's EMODnet reader refuses any line not CB; the same rule here keeps 4,444 (CB) or 8,731 (CB+UN).

emodnet_beach_litter.units_as_published: abundance = item COUNT per survey per litter type; survey_length in m (100 m: 7,252; 1000 m: 2,078; 33 m: 1,081; null: 3,200; 0: 16); survey_width null for 13,897
emodnet_beach_litter.plastic_separable: yes: every survey lists EVERY type of its reference list with explicit zeros (128 lines per OSPAR survey, 216 TSG-ML, 183 JLIST, 82 UNEP_MARLIN, 77 UNEP, 59 ITA, 25 OSPAR_1000). Material follows from the list's own category blocks (OSPAR 1-48 & 112-117 & 121 plastic/polystyrene; TSG-ML G1-G124 'artificial polymer'; JLIST names say 'plastic'/'foamed'; UNEP PL*/FP*; ITA IT1-IT19). My provisional classifier gives plastic 80.4% of 8,610,855 items, ambiguous 0.99%; per-survey plastic share p10/p50/p90 = 0.43/0.78/0.97. No machine-readable material map was found: https://nodc.ogs.it/marinelitter/vocab (200) lists beach attributes but not litter types -> the adapter must commit its own code->material table and say so
gotchas: ERDDAP stores abundance as SHORT: survey 27140 (Edsvik 2017-05-02, type 32, 153,702 pieces of string) reads NaN from ERDDAP; 5 lines exceed 32,767 -> read the zip, not ERDDAP
OSPAR + OSPAR_1000 pairs: 1,534 beach-dates carry both a 100 m all-items survey and a 1 km large-items (> 50 cm) survey - different quantities, keep both under distinct protocol qc
survey_length null on 3,200 (OSPAR 2,599) and 0 on 16 -> per-100 m density needs the protocol default (OSPAR 100 m) under a 'length assumed' qc bit, or the row is dropped
70 surveys (BE 35, PT 23, DE 12) have no location AND no survey start coordinate -> refuse and count
survey start vs beach location: median 0.0001 km, 6 > 10 km, max 270 km (survey 17202: location 54.35N 18.84E, start 54.02N 14.73E) -> position from location, flag disagreement > 5 km
10 location codes carry more than one coordinate
string 'NULL' for missing values throughout

qc_uint8.bits_0_3_protocol: 1 OSPAR-100m, 2 OSPAR-1km large items, 3 TSG-ML/JLIST (MSFD), 4 UNEP/UNEP_MARLIN, 5 ITA, 6 MDMAP 2.0, 7 MDMAP standing stock, 8 MDMAP accumulation, 9 Nurdle Patrol, 10 sand core

qc_uint8.bit_6: survey length assumed from protocol default

proposed_design.platform: hash of source|beach code (EMODnet location_code, MDMAP shoreline_site_id, nurdle rounded position)
proposed_design.precedence_dedup: No cross-source copies were measured, so no precedence drop is needed; within sources: EMODnet European file only; keep OSPAR/OSPAR_1000 pairs as two rows; MDMAP one row per survey_id; drop and count: 70 EMODnet surveys with no position, 16 length-0, 6 zero-minute patrols, 8 width-9999 and 26 width-0 MDMAP transects from area channels. A future second copy of any source (e.g. OSPAR's own database) yields to EMODnet on same beach code + date
proposed_design.licence_split: PUBLIC: Nurdle Patrol + sand rows (CC0) and EMODnet CB (+UN if accepted) surveys; PRIVATE until resolved: EMODnet LS surveys (8,130; SeaDataNet licence clause 5) and all MDMAP (no stated licence)
falsifiable_checks: MDMAP: sum of the seven material totals equals total_debris_items and plastic <= total on every transect (measured 22,509 of 22,509 today) - a single failure refuses the store
EMODnet: every survey of reference list L has exactly len(L) type lines with zeros explicit (measured: 128/216/82/25/59/183/77, except 27 two-list surveys with 399) - refuse on any other count
Nurdle: recomputing pellets per 10 min as count*10/minutes reproduces the published standardised value on >= 7,275 rows (measured) - if the formula match falls, the source changed its rule
round trip: the store's de-logged log_items_100m for every EMODnet survey equals sum(abundance)/length*100 from the zip within float16 error (log10 quantisation ~ 1e-3 relative)

external, measured and NOT reproduced: EEA's EU coastline baseline (287 items/100 m 2015-16, 203 in 2020-21) - the public EMODnet subset gives median-of-beach-medians 124-158 and no 29% fall, so this cannot be a falsifier for this subset; record it, do not use it
